meta.title: Cosmoria
meta.description: Command a colony on a distant planet: lay out its walkways, bring in water and food, open workshops and shows, and watch the shelters turn into domes.
meta.titre_seo: Cosmoria: build a space colony, free city-building game
meta.description_seo: Build a colony on a red planet: walkways, water, greenhouses, workshops, cores and shows. Your colonists move up from shelters to domes. Free, for ages 12+.
meta.presentation: Cosmoria is a city-building game where you command a space colony seen from above, in relief. You lay out walkways and housing zones, then colonists arrive along the spaceport track and inflate their shelters. Everything travels along the walkways: market sellers, security officers, mediators, teachers, doctors and artists make their rounds in spacesuits, and every home they serve grows, from an inflatable shelter to an arcology. Greenhouses, mines and workshops supply food, ceramics, furniture, clothing and nectar, which convoys and freighters trade with the colonies of the sector. You keep an eye on fire, work, taxes and safety, keep five Minds happy and answer to the Earth Council; when raiders attack, you raise squads. The campaign has 17 maps over 10 tiers and three worlds: red Rubra, icy Boreas and golden Amber.
meta.regles: Every mission sets its targets: a number of residents, then ratings for culture, prosperity and peace, plus the Council's trust. On a computer, open a category on the left, take a building, then click or drag on the ground; right-click shows its sheet, the scroll wheel zooms, the arrow keys move the view, R rotates it and P or Esc pauses. On a touch screen, swipe to draw and tap Confirm; with two fingers you pan and zoom, and a long press opens it. Three stars per mission: win, do without emergency aid from Earth, and finish before the target date. A ruined colony or a command withdrawn by the Council loses the mission. To lead a squad, tap its base, then "Send" and a spot on the map.
meta.competences: colony planning, budget management, anticipating risks, reading data
meta.jaquette_alt: A large glass dome sheltering buildings and trees, surrounded by white pods and astronauts on red ground

textes.titre.sousTitre: Build the colony of the stars
textes.titre.consigne: Lay out walkways and housing zones, then meet your colonists' needs: water, food, cores, shows. Every need you meet makes their homes grow and fills your treasury.
textes.outil.verrouille: The tutorial will unlock this building later.

textes.outil.aideSouris: {nom}: click or drag on the map; right-click or Esc to drop the tool.

textes.bat.logement.aide: Newcomers settle here in an inflatable shelter, then the home grows once its needs are met.
textes.bat.deblayer.aide: Removes resin trees, buildings, walkways and wrecks, with no refund.
textes.bat.route.aide: Every walker travels on walkways: how you lay them out makes or breaks your colony.
textes.bat.barriere.aide: Stops walkers on their rounds and lets through those headed somewhere.
textes.bat.puits.aide: Gives drill water to homes within 2 tiles. Needs no workers and no walkway.
textes.bat.fontaine.aide: Gives pure water within 4 tiles. Must be within 10 tiles of a full pumping station.
textes.bat.reservoir.aide: Fills up at the water's edge, or through a pipeline from a full station, and feeds pure-water posts.
textes.bat.aqueduc.aide: Carries water from one pumping station to another. It can pass over a walkway.
textes.bat.ferme_ble.aide: Goes on fertile soil. Its cart pushers take the grain to the nearest food silo.
textes.bat.grenier.aide: Holds up to 24 loads of food for the markets.
textes.bat.marche.aide: Its buyer goes to the food silo or warehouse, and its seller stocks up the homes she passes.
textes.bat.temple_ceres.aide: Its mediator links the homes he passes to Florea, the Mind of crops.
textes.bat.theatre.aide: When an artist arrives, it puts on a 32-day show: its holo-artists bring 15 entertainment points.
textes.bat.colonie_acteurs.aide: Trains artists and sends them to the nearest holotheatre that needs one.
textes.bat.forum.aide: Its tax collector walks past the homes and collects the tax they have owed since his last visit.
textes.bat.prefecture.aide: Its security officer lowers fire risk and rushes to put out fires within 15 tiles.
textes.bat.ingenieur.aide: Its technician repairs the buildings he passes and prevents breakdowns.
textes.bat.ruines.aide: What's left after a fire. Clear it to rebuild.
textes.bat.gravats.aide: What's left after a breakdown. Clear it to rebuild.
textes.bat.incendie.aide: Fire can spread to nearby buildings. A security officer puts it out in 2 days.
textes.cause.sansPreneur: storage full, nowhere to send it (silo, warehouse or workshop)
textes.info.terrainVague: Vacant plot: newcomers will settle here if there's room left and they like the colony.
textes.info.recensee: Tax collector came by recently: taxes collected
textes.info.nonRecensee: No tax collector for a long time: taxes are piling up (one year at most)
textes.info.bientot: All set: the home is about to grow.
textes.marcheur.immigrant.aide: Come in by the spaceport track and settle wherever there's room.
textes.marcheur.emigrant.aide: Unhappy with the colony and leaving the map.
textes.marcheur.sansabri.aide: Their home burned down or shrank: they're looking for a new one, or else they'll leave.
textes.marcheur.livreur.aide: Pushes a hover cart holding one load of goods.
textes.marcheur.acheteuse.aide: Brings one load of food from the food silo back to the market.
textes.marcheur.vendeuse.aide: Stocks up the homes she passes, with up to 4 months of food.
textes.marcheur.prefet.aide: Lowers the fire risk of the buildings he passes and puts out fires.
textes.marcheur.percepteur.aide: Collects the tax each home has built up since his last visit (one year at most).
textes.marcheur.pretre.aide: Links the homes he passes to the Mind of his core.
textes.marcheur.acteur.aide: Goes from the artists' studio to the holotheatre for a new show.
textes.marcheur.comedien.aide: Brings the holotheatre's show to the homes he passes.
textes.terrain.prairieAide: The only ground where crops can go.
textes.terrain.eauAide: A pumping station built on the shore fills up by itself.
textes.terrain.romeAide: Newcomers and leavers pass through here. It can't be removed.
textes.conseil.immigrationArretee: Mood is too low: nobody wants to move in any more.
textes.calque.eauAide: Light blue: drill water. Dark blue: pure water from posts. The columns show the water at each home.
textes.calque.feuAide: The taller and redder the column, the bigger the fire threat. Only security officers stay visible.
textes.calque.dommagesAide: The taller and redder the column, the more likely the building is to give way. Only technicians stay visible.
textes.calque.stocksAide: Food silos, markets and warehouses: the taller and greener the column, the fuller they are; red means almost empty. Only cart pushers, hauliers, buyers and sellers stay visible.
textes.tuto.ostie.1: Open “Housing” and lay out 10 housing tiles within 2 tiles of the spaceport track.
textes.tuto.ostie.2: Newcomers come in by the spaceport track. Wait until you have 24 residents (you can speed up time with +).
textes.tuto.ostie.3: The shelters are thirsty: open “Water” and place 2 ice drills in the middle of your homes.
textes.tuto.ostie.4: With water, a small inflatable shelter becomes a large inflatable shelter. Wait until you have 6.
textes.tuto.ostie.5: You need food: place a grain greenhouse on fertile soil (the terraformed moss), near a walkway.
textes.tuto.ostie.6: Grain goes to a silo: build a food silo linked to the greenhouse by a walkway.
textes.tuto.ostie.7: Build a market near the homes: its buyer will go to the silo, and its seller will feed the homes.
textes.tuto.ostie.8: Once fed, shelters turn into pods. Grow 5 homes into small pods (long-press a home to see what it's missing).
textes.tuto.ostie.9: Final goal: reach 150 residents. Add homes, drills and a 2nd market if needed.
textes.tuto.pompei.1: Shelters catch fire easily: open “Security” and build a security post along a walkway.
textes.tuto.pompei.2: Without upkeep, buildings end up giving way: build a maintenance workshop.
textes.tuto.pompei.3: To collect tax, build a colony office: its tax collector takes the tax of the homes he walks past.
textes.tuto.pompei.4: Build a core of Florea near the pods. Grow 8 homes into large pods.
textes.tuto.pompei.5: Place a pumping station on the riverbank, link it by pipeline to a station in the colony, then add pure-water posts around it. Grow 8 homes into small modules.
textes.tuto.pompei.6: Build an artists' studio and a holotheatre: their shows will grow 8 homes into large modules.
textes.tuto.pompei.7: Final goal: reach 600 residents. Keep an eye on mood and tax in Command.
textes.tuto.fini: Tutorial complete: the colony is yours.

textes.missions.bientotAide: This sector is coming in a future version of the game.
textes.mission.ostie.intro: Earth is opening its first camp on Rubra. On this empty coast, by the sea, welcome your first colonists: shelters, water, food. The tutorial guides you step by step.
textes.mission.pompei.intro: At the foot of the old sleeping volcano, the colony grows fast and overheats just as fast. Protect it from fires and breakdowns, collect tax, and give it a core, pure-water posts and a holotheatre.
textes.briefing.etoiles: 1 star for winning, 1 without Earth's emergency aid, 1 if you win in {mois} months or less.

textes.mission.ravenne.intro: On the edge of Rubra's lagoons, Lagunaris must become a colony of craftspeople. Get its workshops going, sell your ceramics to the neighbouring colonies and answer the Council's requests.
textes.mission.narbo.intro: Meridia, the young colony of southern Rubra, opens onto the sea. Make weapons, build a cargo dock and send your freighters to Tarrena and Alba Prima.
textes.mission.massalia.intro: Port-Thalassa, Rubra's great freighter port. Fish, weave clothing, sell it across the Federation and turn the colony into a rich and cultured place.

textes.bat.residence_palais.aide: The commander's tower: the strongest desirability in the colony. Only one commander's home per colony.
textes.bat.hippodrome.aide: Antigrav races give 30 entertainment points to the homes its pilots pass. It needs racers from the workshop. Only one per colony.
textes.bat.fabrique_chars.aide: Builds antigrav racers and sends them to the circuit.
textes.bat.muraille.aide: Stops enemies, who must break it down or go around it. A fortified airlock lets a walkway through.
textes.bat.tour.aide: Built against an energy rampart, it fires on enemies within 6 tiles. It needs staff.
textes.bat.porte.aide: Built across a walkway: residents pass, enemies must break it down.
textes.bat.caserne.aide: Trains a recruit every 8 days for the first incomplete base. An armoured guard takes one load of weapons.
textes.bat.academie_militaire.aide: Recruits pass through it before reaching their base and gain one training level.
textes.bat.fort_legionnaires.aide: Holds 16 armoured guards, heavy and tough up close. Tap the base to give an order. 6 bases at most.
textes.bat.fort_javelots.aide: Holds 16 marksmen, who hit their target from 5 tiles. Tap the base to give an order. 6 bases at most.
textes.bat.fort_cavaliers.aide: Holds 16 jet-bike riders, fast to harass the enemy. Tap the base to give an order. 6 bases at most.
textes.refus.unique: There can only be one per colony.
textes.refus.fortsMax: The colony already has 6 bases, the maximum.
textes.refus.muraille: A turret must be built against an energy rampart.
textes.refus.moral: The squad's morale is too low: it is returning to base.
textes.refus.soldats: This squad has no guards available.

textes.difficulte.facileAide: Higher starting funds, fewer enemies, buildings that wear out more slowly, a more patient Council and Minds.
textes.difficulte.normalAide: The game as the mission intends it.
textes.difficulte.difficileAide: Lower starting funds, more enemies, buildings that wear out faster, a more demanding Council and Minds.

armee.troupesAbsentes.other: {effectif} guards are defending the Federation; back in about {n} months.

msg.villa.other: A home becomes a residence: {n} colonists leave to find a new home.

textes.msg.arrestation: A security officer arrested a thief.

msg.invasionAnnonce.other: {faction}: a raid of {effectif} enemies is nearing the colony. It will arrive in {n} months.

textes.msg.invasionFuite: The enemy has lost too much: it is retreating.
textes.msg.invasionRepoussee: Raid repelled without a single building destroyed! Peace rises.

msg.invasionFinie.one: The raid is over; {d} building was destroyed.
msg.invasionFinie.other: The raid is over; {d} buildings were destroyed.

msg.legionsAnnonce.other: The Council has lost patience: Earth Forces arrive in {n} months to strip you of command.

textes.msg.legionsRepoussees: Earth Forces are driven back. The Council gives you one last chance.

msg.demandeTroupes.other: The Council asks for {force} guards within {n} months (Command, Council tab).

msg.demandeTroupesRappel.other: Reminder: the Council awaits {force} guards, {n} months left.

textes.msg.demandeTroupesRefusee: No squad was sent: the Council is displeased.

msg.troupesParties.other: {n} guards leave to defend the Federation.

msg.troupesVictoire.other: Victory! The squad returns with {n} guards ({morts} out of action); the Council is satisfied.

msg.troupesDefaite.other: Defeat: the squad returns with {n} guards ({morts} out of action); the Council is disappointed.

textes.mission.aquilee.intro: Aquilon guards the great pass of Boreas, the ice moon. The Canyon Raiders are coming down from the ridges: build barracks and a base before they arrive, make weapons for Verenia and turn the outpost into a real colony.
textes.mission.vindobona.intro: On the frozen river of Boreas, Vindara holds the frontier against the Frost Clans. Their bands grow year after year: raise full squads, train them and answer the Council's calls.
textes.mission.ephese.intro: Ephyra, Rubra's learned port, built around its great core, dreams of rivalling Sophia. Fertile soil is scarce here: bring grain in by sea, build schools, media libraries and holotheatres, and make it a capital of culture.
textes.mission.burdigala.intro: On the banks of Rubra's great river, Burgalis lives off its berries. Fertile soil is scarce and bands of raiders come down from the northern canyons: plant berries, sell your nectar across the sector and keep the colony safe behind its energy ramparts.
textes.mission.alexandrie.intro: Solara stands between the sea and Amber's golden desert. The river feeds only a narrow strip of soil: buy grain from Dunara, post security officers everywhere, since fire spreads fast under the two suns, and make the colony the most learned in the Federation.
textes.mission.leptis.intro: Ambrea, the fibre oasis, stretches between the sea and the Amber desert. The Dune Nomads' bikers strike from the south, fast and many: import your grain, weave clothing for Earth and put your bases in their path.
textes.mission.corinthe.intro: Earth is rebuilding Isthmia on the remains of an old camp, between two seas. The ground often shakes here, and whole districts can give way at once: keep credits aside to rebuild and make the colony the great market of Rubra.
textes.mission.colonia.intro: Nivalis guards the ice river of Boreas. On the far bank, the Frost Clans gather ever larger bands, and the bridge is their way in: hold it, raise squads and feed a colony that grows under threat.
textes.mission.antioche.intro: Orontis, Rubra's great metropolis, draws the richest families of the Federation. Build districts for notables, residences then arcologies, surrounded by gardens, cores and shows, and give it an antigrav circuit worthy of it.
textes.mission.palmyre.intro: Miragia, the colony of mirages, lives on the convoys that cross the Amber desert. The Amber Sharpshooters attack from the east, fast on their bikes: protect your drills and walkways, buy your grain and drive back ever larger raids.
textes.mission.athenes.intro: Sophia, capital of knowledge and the arts, awaits its commander. Here everything counts: culture, prosperity, peace and the Council's trust, at the highest thresholds of the campaign. It is your final trial before the title of Regent of Cosmoria.
textes.mission.eburacum.intro: At the edge of the Federation, Ultima holds the ice of Boreas against the Howlers. Their bands come down from the north through the resin forests: build a strong, prosperous colony and become Regent of Cosmoria at the frontier of the known world.
textes.aide.eauRequise: It needs a full pumping station close by.
textes.campagne.texte: You have won all 10 tiers: you are now Regent of Cosmoria. {n} stars out of {max}.
textes.campagne.suite: Replay the other sector of a tier to earn its stars, or build freely on a map you have already won.
textes.aide.debut.texte: Lay walkways from the spaceport track, then housing tiles along them: families arrive by the track and settle. Give them water, food and services so their homes grow. The Summary tab in Command always says what is missing, and tapping a building explains what is holding it back.
textes.aide.routes.texte: Almost every building needs a walkway within 2 tiles. Its workers set out along the walkways: roamers (security officers, mediators, market sellers…) head for the homes and buildings that need them, the most urgent and the nearest first, and serve everything they pass; a walkway with no needs is skipped. The others head straight for their goal. A traffic arch stops roamers but lets everyone else through: it keeps services inside a district.
textes.aide.maisons.texte: A home goes up a level when all its needs are met, and goes down if one of them is missing for too long. From inflatable shelter to dome, each level asks a little more: water, varied food, a link to the Minds, shows, goods, services and a nicer neighbourhood (desirability). Large homes spread over 2 × 2 tiles by absorbing their neighbours. Tap a home: it tells you what it needs to grow.
textes.aide.eau.texte: An ice drill gives water to nearby homes. A pure-water post, which is better, must be linked to a full pumping station. A station fills up beside a river or the sea, or through a pipeline coming from another station that has water. Thermal baths need a station too. The “Water” overlay shows what is covered.
textes.aide.nourriture.texte: Crops (greenhouses, orchard, protein farm) go on fertile soil: the richer it is, the more they produce. Their carts deliver to the nearest food silo; the market buyer fetches food there and the market sellers carry it to the homes. Rich homes want several foods. Without fertile soil, buy grain from neighbouring colonies: it arrives in the warehouses, then goes to the silos.
textes.aide.travail.texte: Residents of working age fill the jobs; a building short of workers slows down or stops. When hands are short, the priorities (Command, Work tab) decide who is served first. Unemployment, high tax or wages below Earth's lower the mood, and unhappy residents leave. Notables do not work.
textes.aide.industrie.texte: A dredge, a mine, a resin harvester, a fibre field or a berry plantation produces a material; the workshop next door turns it into goods (ceramics, furniture, clothing, nectar, weapons). Warehouses keep materials and goods; their orders (accept, refuse, fetch, empty) and limits decide what goes in. The market sells goods to the homes that ask for them.
textes.aide.securite.texte: Every building builds up a risk of fire and breakdown: a security officer or a technician walking past resets it. A building that burns or gives way leaves a wreck or debris, and fire sometimes spreads to its neighbours, faster in a dry climate. Poor, unhappy districts attract thieves; security officers arrest them, but high crime turns into riots. The ground can also shake and flatten a district.
textes.aide.finances.texte: Every month, each occupied home owes that month's tax, at the rate set in Command; the colony office's tax collector takes everything it owes when he walks past (one year of arrears at most). Wages, building, purchases, festivals and the contribution to Earth come out of the treasury, and sales to other colonies go in. Below zero, Earth bails the treasury out once (emergency aid), which costs the second star; debt costs interest, and beyond 5,000 credits of debt nothing more can be built.
textes.aide.religion.texte: Florea (harvests), Mareo (seas), Nexus (trade), Bastion (defence) and Harmonia (good mood) are the colony's great AIs. Each wants cores, in proportion to the population, and festivals. A delighted Mind grants a favour; a neglected one shuts down and cuts its services: lost harvest, lost freighters, an emptied warehouse, disheartened squads, gloomy mood. The Minds tab in Command shows each one's mood.
textes.aide.culture.texte: Holotheatres, arenas, xenodromes and the antigrav circuit put on shows when their performers come from their school (artists' studio, arena robot workshop, menagerie, racer workshop). Schools, media libraries and science institutes educate residents; hairdressers, thermal baths, doctors and hospitals keep them healthy, or an epidemic may break out. The culture rating counts the places in cores, holotheatres, media libraries, schools and institutes per resident.
textes.aide.commerce.texte: The sector map (Trade button in the top bar) shows the colonies and, next to each one, what it buys and what it sells; opening a route is paid once. For each good, choose: buy, sell, keep or nothing, and how much to keep. Convoys call at the warehouses near the colony entrance; freighters moor at the cargo dock. Each colony trades a limited amount per year.
textes.aide.empereur.texte: The Council's trust drops a little every year. It rises when you meet its requests on time (goods, credits, troops) and when you make it a gift from your personal fortune. Your commander's salary adds to that fortune, which you keep from one mission to the next. If trust stays too low for too long, the Council sends Earth Forces against your colony.
textes.aide.cotes.texte: A mission is won when the population and the four ratings (culture, prosperity, peace, trust) reach their thresholds together. Prosperity is recalculated in January: profit, jobs, wages, rich homes, varied food; it never goes above the average value of the homes. Peace rises each year without riots or destruction. The Ratings tab in Command says what holds each one back.
textes.aide.armee.texte: A raid is announced on the sector map a few months before it arrives. The barracks train recruits with weapons; each base raises a squad of 16 guards (armoured guards, marksmen or jet-bike riders), which the defence academy trains. Tap a base to give an order: go, change formation, return. Energy ramparts, turrets and fortified airlocks stop or slow the enemy.
textes.aide.patriciens.texte: Beyond the dome, wealthy families build residences and then arcologies, from 2 × 2 to 4 × 4 tiles: they ask for nectar, a hospital, several Minds, great shows and a very fine neighbourhood. They pay a lot of tax but do not work: you need enough colonists to keep the colony running. The Council Hall, the commander's quarters and the antigrav circuit round off a great colony.
textes.voisins.intro: Found a sector together: each player builds their own colony on their own device, at their own pace, and you trade as neighbours. The sector wins when every active colony reaches its goals.
textes.voisins.pleine: This sector is full: all 4 colonies are taken.
textes.voisins.serveur: The exchange is not answering. Shared sectors are played on freemicrogames.com, with a connection.
textes.voisins.codeInvalide: This code doesn't look right: 6 letters or digits.
textes.voisins.codeAide: Give this code to your friends: each one takes a free colony in the sector, whenever they like. They can also use the Friends page of the site.
textes.voisins.enLigne: Online: trade with your neighbours is open.
textes.voisins.horsLigne: Offline: routes to your neighbours are closed.
textes.voisins.gagneeTexte: Every active colony has reached its goals. Well done, commanders!

voisins.reserve.one: {n} load is waiting at the airlock for warehouse space.
voisins.reserve.other: {n} loads are waiting at the airlock for warehouse space.

textes.voisins.absent: No visit for more than 7 days: a computer colony trades in their place; their stall stays open.
textes.voisins.envoyerSignal: Send a signal to your neighbours
textes.voisins.part: {nom}: {pop} residents, {ventes} credits of sales to neighbours
textes.voisins.ficheJoueur: The colony of a player in your sector: you trade through the exchange, at the price between players.

textes.signal.route: Open a route to my colony.
textes.province.campanie.desc: The grain and berries of Opalys, the fishing port of Port-Nacre, the crystal and fibre of Nolune, the resin trees of Sylvara.
textes.province.hispanie.desc: The fish-rich coast of Sagune, the grain plains of Valoria, the resin trees of Dertane, the metal and crystal of Ilerys.

msg.prov.livraison.other: A convoy from {voisin} brings {n} loads ({deniers} credits).

textes.msg.prov.enLigne: Sector exchange reached: routes to your neighbours are open.
textes.msg.prov.horsLigne: Exchange unreachable: routes to your neighbours are closed.
textes.msg.prov.objectif: Your colony has reached its goals! The sector wins when every active colony reaches them.
textes.sauve.provinceSeule: A shared-sector colony saves itself, in its sector: done.

textes.conseil.impotsAttente: Tax to collect in homes: {n} credits
textes.commerce.toucheCite: Tap a colony on the map: its sheet opens here, with the price of the route.
textes.missions.carteAide: Tap a colony on the map to read its mission. The number is its tier; gold colonies are won.

tutoB.nouveauxIntro.one: In this mission you can build {n} building you don't know yet. Tap it to learn what it does and what to do.
tutoB.nouveauxIntro.other: In this mission you can build {n} buildings you don't know yet. Tap one to learn what it does and what to do.

textes.tutoB.menuAide: In the menu, the "New" mark stays on the ones you haven't read yet.
textes.tutoB.route: Place it within 2 tiles of a walkway: its workers and cart pushers go that way.
textes.tutoB.employes: It needs {n} workers: they come from occupied homes, so you need enough residents (Command, Work tab).
textes.tutoB.prairie: Place it on fertile soil (the terraformed moss): the more fertile the soil, the bigger the harvest.
textes.tutoB.pres.arbres: Place it right next to resin trees: its harvesters collect their resin.
textes.tutoB.pres.eau: Place it on the shore (river or sea): that's where silica is dredged.
textes.tutoB.pres.rochers: Place it against rocks (big blocks of stone): the rock is dug there.
textes.tutoB.fermeAliment: Its harvest ({bien}) goes to the nearest food silo: build a silo linked by a walkway, then a market near the homes.
textes.tutoB.fermeMatiere: Its harvest ({bien}) goes to the warehouse; a "{atelier}" building turns it into {produit}, which markets sell or you export.
textes.tutoB.extraction: Output: {bien} ({n} loads a year), to be stored in the warehouse: build a warehouse linked by a walkway.
textes.tutoB.versAtelier: A "{atelier}" building turns this material ({bien}) into {produit}.
textes.tutoB.vendre: You can also sell it to other colonies (Trade button at the top).
textes.tutoB.atelier: Material: {matiere}. Product: {produit}. The material comes from "{source}" or is bought from other colonies.
textes.tutoB.atelierImport: Material: {matiere}. Product: {produit}. Here the material is bought from other colonies (Trade button at the top).
textes.tutoB.entrepotAtelier: You need a warehouse linked by a walkway: its hauliers bring the material to the workshop and take away what it makes.
textes.tutoB.peche: Place it on the shore, near a shoal of fish (ripples in the water): its barge goes fishing.
textes.tutoB.pecheGrenier: The fish goes to the food silo, like grain: you need a silo and a market.
textes.tutoB.entrepot1: It stores materials and goods (8 slots): workshops, markets and convoys come to use it.
textes.tutoB.entrepot2: Put it near the colony entrance for trade; tap it to set what it accepts, refuses or fetches.
textes.tutoB.grenier: Crops and fishers deliver food here; market buyers come to collect it. Put it between the crops and the districts.
textes.tutoB.marche1: Put it among the homes: its seller goes from home to home, first where things are most lacking.
textes.tutoB.marche2: Its buyer fetches food from the food silo and goods from the warehouse (40 walkway tiles at most).
textes.tutoB.service: Its worker ({marcheur}) sets out along the walkways to the homes that need him and serves everything within 2 tiles: put it in the heart of the district.
textes.tutoB.prefet: The security officer lowers the fire risk and runs to put out fires. Build one post in each district: the "Fire risk" overlay shows buildings in danger.
textes.tutoB.ingenieur: Its technician repairs buildings; without him they wear out and then give way. The "Wear" overlay shows where he is missing.
textes.tutoB.impot: Its tax collector takes the tax each home has owed since his last visit: without him, no tax (rate in Command).
textes.tutoB.religion: Homes need cores to grow, and {dieu} wants enough cores to stay in a good mood (Command, Minds tab).
textes.tutoB.education: Homes need it to go up a level: tap a home to see what it is missing.
textes.tutoB.sante: Homes need it to go up a level, and the colony is better protected from epidemics.
textes.tutoB.marbre: You also need {n} loads of crystal in a warehouse to build it (crystal mine or purchase).
textes.tutoB.eau: It needs a full pumping station close by.
textes.tutoB.spectacle: It needs artists: also build "{ecoles}". They come to perform here, then its worker ({marcheur}) brings the show to the homes.
textes.tutoB.ecoleArt: It prepares artists ({artiste}), who go to perform in "{lieux}": build them on the same walkway network.
textes.tutoB.puits: It gives water to homes within 2 tiles. No walkway or workers needed: put one in the middle of each group of shelters.
textes.tutoB.fontaine: Place it within 10 tiles of a full pumping station: it gives pure water to homes within 4 tiles, which they need to grow.
textes.tutoB.reservoir1: Put it on the edge of a river, lake or the sea so it fills up; or link it by pipeline to an already full station.
textes.tutoB.reservoir2: A full pumping station feeds pure-water posts and thermal baths within 10 tiles ("Water" overlay).
textes.tutoB.aqueduc: Draw it from a full pumping station to another station: the water flows through it. It can pass over a walkway.
textes.tutoB.deco: It beautifies the district: nearby homes gain desirability, which they need to move up.
textes.tutoB.place: Draw it on an existing walkway: the walkway stays usable and the neighbouring homes become nicer.
textes.tutoB.barriere: Put it on a walkway: it stops workers on their rounds (security officers, sellers…) and keeps them in their district; cart pushers and residents pass.
textes.tutoB.residence: They make the surroundings very desirable: put them in the heart of the fine districts. Only one per colony.
textes.tutoB.oracle: It links to all Five Minds at once, with no walkway or workers: put it where it beautifies homes.
textes.tutoB.quai1: Place it on the shore, one side on the water: freighters on sea routes dock there.
textes.tutoB.quai2: Then open a sea route (Trade button at the top); its dockers carry loads between the freighter and the warehouses.
textes.tutoB.caserne: It trains the recruits for your bases; an armoured guard takes a load of weapons: keep weapons in a warehouse (armoury or purchase).
textes.tutoB.academieMil: Recruits pass through it before joining their base and fight better: put it between the barracks and the bases.
textes.tutoB.fort: It holds a squad of 16 guards ({unite}), trained by the barracks. Tap the base to give an order: go, formation, return.
textes.tutoB.tour: Put it against an energy rampart: its crew fires on enemies within 6 tiles.
textes.tutoB.muraille: Draw it around the colony, on the side enemies come from (sector map): they must break it down or go around.
textes.tutoB.porte: Put it across a walkway that goes through the rampart: residents pass, enemies must break it down.
textes.tutoB.calque: To see where its worker goes, open the overlays (button at the top): the building stays visible, and so does the worker.
